findings.explanation: The Cisco EoX Support API is served at https://apix.cisco.com/supporttools/eox/rest/5/EOXByProductID/{pageIndex}/{productID} (with sibling EOXBySerialNumber / EOXBySWReleaseString methods). The URL given does not exist, so the lookup refresh step cannot be built as written.
findings.quote: schedule a weekly refresh from **Cisco EoX API** responses at https://api.cisco.com/software/eol/v2/lifecycle/products
findings.suggested_fix: Use GET https://apix.cisco.com/supporttools/eox/rest/5/EOXByProductID/1/{PID list}?responseencoding=json, and map LastDateOfSupport.value to ldos_date and EndOfSaleDate.value to eos_date.

findings.explanation: In NDFC 12 automation (for example the cisco.dcnm collection), the all-switch inventory is usually .../lan-fabric/rest/inventory/allswitches and the per-fabric roster .../control/fabrics/{fabric}/inventory/switchesByFabric. Neither path as written is confirmed in the NDFC API reference.
findings.suggested_fix: Check both paths against the NDFC 12.x LAN Fabric API reference and correct them in dataSources, implementation and detailedImplementation.

findings.explanation: The NDFC API and NDFC configuration guide references point at the site roots developer.cisco.com/docs/ and cisco.com/c/en/us/, so a reader cannot reach the cited documents.
findings.quote: "title": "Cisco NDFC Fabric Controller configuration guide — inventory and LAN fabric operations", "url": "https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/"
findings.suggested_fix: Link the NDFC 12.x REST API reference and the 'LAN Fabric > Switches / Inventory' chapter of the NDFC configuration guide.

findings.explanation: The NDFC 12 train ran 12.0 to 12.2.x before NDFC folded into unified Nexus Dashboard 4.x. '12.4.x' may not be a real NDFC release.
findings.suggested_fix: Cite a real NDFC release (for example 12.1.3 / 12.2.x) or the Nexus Dashboard 4.x unified release.

findings.explanation: NX-OS logs to facility local7 by default, and sibling UCs 18.4.5/18.4.6 say local7. dataSources repeats local6.
findings.quote: forward facility=local6 lines from NDFC and switches
findings.suggested_fix: Say local7 (the NX-OS default), or tell readers to match the facility on their `logging server` command.

findings.explanation: The reviewer is an automated agent, two of the four reg_risk lanes can never fire, and the EoX URL is wrong. The UC was not exercised end to end.
findings.suggested_fix: Downgrade status until the SPL and the lookup refresh have been tested.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: reg_risk is evaluated after `stats ... latest(managed_key) AS managed_status latest(oper_key) AS oper_status ... BY dev_name`, but it tests `managed_key` and `oper_key`. Those fields no longer exist after stats, so 'registration_gap' and 'reachability_alert' can never be assigned. Test `managed_status` and `oper_status` instead.

`dev_name=coalesce(hostname, host, ...)` falls back to Splunk's default `host` metadata, which is always present. On fabric_status and audit events, and on any inventory record missing `hostname`, dev_name becomes the collector's host. Unrelated switches collapse into one row, and spurious eox_lookup_miss rows appear. Because model_key defaults to "", `isnotnull(model)` is always true, so the 'no_model' lane is unreachable.

summary: The inventory and EoX lifecycle design is practical and well explained, but the SPL never raises the registration_gap or reachability_alert lanes because it tests fields that stats has already dropped. It also coalesces Splunk's default `host` field as the device name. The Cisco EoX API URL given for building the lookup is wrong.
